### Problem: path sum {#sec-tr-p3-sum}

::: {.p-statement}
Return true when some root-to-leaf path adds up to `targetSum`.

Constraints: $0 \le n \le 5000$, node values and the target in $[-1000, 1000]$.

Source: [LC 112 · Path Sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/path-sum/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Subtract the node from the remaining target as you go down. A leaf succeeds when the remaining target equals its value. Checking an internal node, or a null child, reports a path that does not end at a leaf.
:::

::: {#fig-tr-sum}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):

    root = V.Node("5", [
        V.Node("4", [
            V.Node("11", [V.Node("7"), V.Node("2", color="amber")], color="amber"),
        ], color="amber"),
        V.Node("8", [V.Node("13"), V.Node("4", [V.Node("1")])]),
    ], color="amber")
    V.tree(ax, p, root, dx=1.05, dy=1.25, size=9)

V.show(draw)
```

Target $22$. The shaded path $5, 4, 11, 2$ meets it at a leaf. $5, 8, 4, 1$ sums to $18$. An internal node whose prefix already equals the target is not a yes.

:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Remaining.** Pass `target - val` to each existing child. A leaf returns whether `val == target`.
2. **Explicit stack.** The same subtraction, stored beside the node. Useful when $n = 5000$ is a path and you do not want the call stack.

**Invariant.** `ok(u, t)` is true exactly when some leaf in the subtree of $u$ is reached with the remaining sum $t$.
:::

The state is the sum still needed. Both children missing is the leaf test.

##### Python

```{python}
def has_path_sum(root, target):
    if root is None:
        return False
    if root.left is None and root.right is None:
        return root.val == target
    return has_path_sum(root.left, target - root.val) or has_path_sum(root.right, target - root.val)
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool hasPathSum(TreeNode* root, int target) {
    if (!root) return false;
    if (!root->left && !root->right) return root->val == target;
    return hasPathSum(root->left, target - root->val) || hasPathSum(root->right, target - root->val);
}
```

:::

#### Stack

::: {.form-next}
Carry `(node, remaining)` on an explicit stack. The leaf test is unchanged.
:::

```{python}

#| renderings: [light, dark]

    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get('sum', 'stack')
    assert str(final) == 'True'
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def has_path_sum_stack(root, target):
    if root is None:
        return False
    st = [(root, target)]
    while st:
        u, t = st.pop()
        if u.left is None and u.right is None and u.val == t:
            return True
        if u.left:
            st.append((u.left, t - u.val))
        if u.right:
            st.append((u.right, t - u.val))
    return False


sample = from_level([5, 4, 8, 11, None, 13, 4, 7, 2, None, None, None, 1])
assert has_path_sum(sample, 22) and has_path_sum_stack(sample, 22)
assert not has_path_sum(from_level([1, 2, 3]), 5)
assert not has_path_sum(None, 0)
assert has_path_sum(Node(0), 0) and not has_path_sum(Node(1), 0)
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool hasPathSumStack(TreeNode* root, int target) {
    if (!root) return false;
    vector<pair<TreeNode*, int>> st = {{root, target}};
    while (!st.empty()) {
        auto [u, t] = st.back();
        st.pop_back();
        if (!u->left && !u->right && u->val == t) return true;
        if (u->left) st.push_back({u->left, t - u->val});
        if (u->right) st.push_back({u->right, t - u->val});
    }
    return false;
}
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
$O(n)$ time. $O(h)$ stack. The empty tree is false for every target, including $0$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- A single node $0$ with target $0$ is true. The empty tree with target $0$ is false.
- `[1,2]` and target $1$ is false: $1$ is not a leaf. The path $1 \to 2$ sums to $3$.
- Negative values mean a prefix equal to the target is not a reason to stop. Only a leaf decides.
- `[-2,null,-3]` with target $-5$ is true. A search that returns false as soon as the remaining target is negative rejects that path.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Testing the target on a null child accepts `[1, 2]` with target $1$. The path has to end at a leaf.
- Returning false when the remaining target goes negative rejects `[-2, null, -3]` with target $-5$.
- The empty tree has no path, so target $0$ is false.
:::

**Variants.** Every root-to-leaf path with that sum is [LC 113 · Path Sum II](https://leetcode.com/problems/path-sum-ii/){difficulty="Medium"}. Listing every path, with no sum to test, is @sec-tr-p3-paths. A binary number read down the path is [LC 1022 · Sum of Root To Leaf Binary Numbers](https://leetcode.com/problems/sum-of-root-to-leaf-binary-numbers/){difficulty="Easy"}. Deleting every node whose paths are all too small is [LC 1080 · Insufficient Nodes in Root to Leaf Paths](https://leetcode.com/problems/insufficient-nodes-in-root-to-leaf-paths/){difficulty="Medium"}. A path that may end anywhere tests the remaining target at every node, not only at a leaf.
